title: What is known about 1RB1LD_1RC0LE_1LA1RE_0LF1LA_1RB0RB_---0LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_1RC0LE_1LA1RE_0LF1LA_1RB0RB_---0LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. After 1.1·106 steps the left end of the tape never moves again. The tape is a fixed left part, a reserve block (011)^k, a counter, and a block of ones at the right end. Each tick a hole runs across the ones and back, and the counter changes near its right end. The counter grows only like the logarithm of the time, and it grows by eating the reserve from the right (k = 481, 476, 472, 468 at 7·106, 4·107, 2·108, 109 steps). The two sweeps are proved in Lean. What happens when the reserve runs out is far beyond simulation.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 49,014 cells have been visited and 48,508 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.454).

claims.title: The sweeps across the ones
claims.text: Going right, a hole 00 moves across (111)^n, three cells every five steps (hole). Going left, the head runs across the ones in states D and A, one cell a step (run_left). Both hold for every n and every tape around.

claims.title: The left end is fixed and the counter eats the reserve
claims.text: In the first 109 steps, the leftmost cell visited is last reached at step 1,072,561. From then on, the 1,621 cells left of the block of ones read: a fixed part, the reserve (011)^k, then the counter. The reserve has k = 481, 476, 474, 472, 470 at steps 7.4·106, 3.7·107, 9.1·107, 1.7·108, 4.0·108, and 468 at 109. Over the same times the counter has 94, 109, 115, 121, 127 cells.

claims.title: A counter that carries
claims.text: Over 5,240 ticks in the first 4·10<sup>8</sup> steps, how far back from the ones a tick changes the tape falls off roughly geometrically. 2,618 ticks change at most 10 cells, 219 reach 30–39 cells back, 19 reach 80–89, and 2 reach 120–129.

claims.title: When the reserve runs out
claims.text: The counter takes about 2 units of the reserve each time the time grows by a factor of about 2.4. At that rate the remaining 468 units last until about 10<sup>90</sup> steps. Only then does the counter reach the fixed left part, where something new must happen. The machine halts only when D reads 0 and the cell to its left is also 0 (F reading 0 is its only undefined transition). Before then, the counter's digits would have to produce the pattern, and their rules are not worked out.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The open part is the counter's carry rules, and what happens when the reserve block is used up.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. After about a million steps the left end of this machine's tape stops moving. Between it and a growing block of ones sits a counter, which grows like the logarithm of the time and eats into a reserve block of the word 011. This page runs the real machine in your browser and explains the pieces. The sweeps are proved in Lean.

facts.text: Across the block of ones, for every length, proved in Lean.
The reserve block (011)^k between 7·10<sup>6</sup> and 10<sup>9</sup> steps.
Steps until the counter could use up the reserve, at its present rate.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.454).
After 109 steps the tape spans 49,014 cells (6 left of the start, 36,320 right), with a density of 1s of 0.99.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: A reserve, a counter and a conveyor
html: Watch the head when it turns in state B just left of the block of ones. From step 1,072,561 on the tape always looks like
0 a 1^6 a 1^6 a^2 1^12 a^14 1^3 a^k [counter] B> 1^N, with a = 011.

The left end never moves again. The block of ones 1N grows by 3 at each visit. The counter is about a hundred cells of ones-runs separated by single 0s. It changes at every tick, mostly near its right end.

A tick is a round trip across the ones. A hole 00 moves right across them, three cells every five steps (hole). At the end the head turns and runs back left in states D and A, one cell a step (run_left). Then it rewrites the counter.

sections.heading: A counter eating its reserve
html: How far back from the ones a tick reaches falls off geometrically, as for a counter's carries. Over 5,240 ticks: 2,618 change at most 10 cells, 1,308 reach 10–19 cells back, 521 reach 20–29, 219 reach 30–39, …, and 2 reach 120–129.
The counter grows only when a carry goes past its left end. It grows into the reserve (011)^k, one unit (three cells) at a time:

sections.heading: What would decide it
html: At the present rate the reserve lasts until about 1090 steps, far beyond any simulation. To decide the machine one needs the counter's digits and carry rules. With those one can see whether some carry can create the halting pattern before the reserve is gone, and what the counter does once it reaches the fixed left part.

summary: A counter that grows leftward into a reserve block of 011s, updated once per tick, while a block of ones at the right end grows; the reserve lasts for about 10^90 steps.
